post.description: Create a new application from a Git repository or Docker image. The application is created with a default web process, auto deploy disabled, and an initial deployment is not triggered automatically - use the Deploy endpoint to start the first deployment. Auto deploy can be enabled later via the Update endpoint but only works with privateGit applications. If Sevalla cannot access the Git repository, the request fails with a 400 error that explains why and links to the page where access can be granted (for example the repository access settings of the GitHub App used by Sevalla).

cluster_id.description: Identifier of the cluster (data center location) where the application will be created.

default_branch.description: Git branch used for deployments. When omitted, the repository default branch is used.

display_name.description: Human-readable name for the new application. Must be between 2 and 64 characters.

docker_image.description: Docker image reference including tag or digest. Required when source is `dockerImage`.

docker_registry_credential_id.description: Identifier of a stored Docker registry credential for pulling private images. Only used when source is `dockerImage`.

git_type.description: Git hosting provider for the repository. `github` - GitHub. `bitbucket` - Bitbucket. `gitlab` - GitLab. Required for private git sources when the provider cannot be auto-detected.

project_id.description: Identifier of the project to group this application under. When omitted, the application is not assigned to any project.

repo_url.description: Full URL of the Git repository. Required when source is `privateGit` or `publicGit`.

source.description: Where the application source code comes from. `privateGit` - private Git repository connected via OAuth. `publicGit` - public Git repository URL. `dockerImage` - Docker container image from a registry.

allow_deploy_paths.description: Glob patterns for file paths that trigger a deployment when changed. When set, only commits touching these paths will trigger auto deploy.

auto_deploy.description: When enabled, a new deployment is automatically triggered on every push to the default branch. Only applies to applications with a private Git connection (privateGit) - has no effect on publicGit or dockerImage applications.

build_cache_enabled.description: When enabled, build artifacts are cached between deployments to speed up subsequent builds

build_path.description: Relative path to the build directory within the repository. Defaults to the repository root.

build_type.description: Build strategy used to build the application. `nixpacks` - auto-detected build system. `railpack` - auto-detected build system, successor to Nixpacks. `dockerfile` - build using a Dockerfile. `pack` - build using Cloud Native Buildpacks. `ingot` - build using a Dockerfile generated from the source code, currently limited to internal testing.

company_id.description: Identifier of the company that owns this application

created_at.description: Timestamp when the application was created, in ISO 8601 format

created_by.description: Identifier of the user who created the application

default_branch.description: Git branch used for automatic and manual deployments when no branch is explicitly specified

display_name.description: Human-readable name shown in the dashboard and API responses

docker_context.description: Docker build context path relative to the repository root. Only applies when build type is `dockerfile`.

docker_image.description: Docker image reference including tag or digest. Only set for applications with `dockerImage` source.

dockerfile_path.description: Relative path to the Dockerfile within the repository. Only applies when build type is `dockerfile`.

git_lfs_enabled.description: When enabled, Git LFS objects are fetched during the source checkout step of a deployment. Enabled by default. Disable this to skip LFS downloads and speed up checkout when the repository contains LFS files that are not needed at build time.

git_type.description: Git hosting provider for the repository. `github` - GitHub. `bitbucket` - Bitbucket. `gitlab` - GitLab. Null for non-git sources.

hibernate_after_seconds.description: Number of seconds of inactivity before the application is hibernated. Only applies when hibernation is enabled.

hibernation_enabled.description: When enabled, the application automatically scales down to zero after a period of inactivity and wakes up on the next incoming request

ignore_deploy_paths.description: Glob patterns for file paths to exclude from deployment triggers. Commits that only touch ignored paths will not trigger auto deploy.

is_suspended.description: Whether the application is currently suspended. Suspended applications have all processes stopped but retain their configuration.

name.description: Unique system name used in URLs and internal references. Auto-generated from the display name and cannot be changed after creation.

namespace.description: Kubernetes namespace where the application workloads run. Assigned automatically during creation.

nixpacks_version.description: Pinned Nixpacks version. When null, the platform default version is used. Only applies when build type is `nixpacks`.

pack_builder.description: Cloud Native Buildpacks builder image. Only applies when build type is `pack`.

project_id.description: Identifier of the project this application is grouped under

repo_url.description: Full URL of the Git repository. Null for Docker image source applications.

source.description: Where the application source code comes from. `privateGit` - private Git repository connected via OAuth. `publicGit` - public Git repository URL. `dockerImage` - Docker container image from a registry. `app` - pipeline promotion target with no Git repository or Docker image connected; deployments arrive by promoting from another pipeline stage.

status.description: Current status of the application reflecting the most recent deployment or lifecycle operation

type.description: Application type. `app` - standard application. `previewApp` - ephemeral preview environment created from a pull request.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the application was last modified, in ISO 8601 format

auto_deploy.description: When enabled, a new deployment is automatically triggered on every push to the default branch. Only applies to applications with a private Git connection (privateGit) - has no effect on publicGit or dockerImage applications.

build_cache_enabled.description: When enabled, build artifacts are cached between deployments to speed up subsequent builds

build_path.description: Relative path to the build directory within the repository. Defaults to the repository root.

build_type.description: Build strategy used to build the application. `nixpacks` - auto-detected build system. `railpack` - auto-detected build system, successor to Nixpacks. `dockerfile` - build using a Dockerfile. `pack` - build using Cloud Native Buildpacks. `ingot` - build using a Dockerfile generated from the source code, currently limited to internal testing.

buildpacks.description: Custom buildpacks configured for this application. Only applies when build type is `pack`.

order.description: Order in which the buildpack is applied during the build

source.description: Buildpack source URL

cluster_id.description: Identifier of the cluster where this application is deployed

company_id.description: Identifier of the company that owns this application

created_at.description: Timestamp when the application was created, in ISO 8601 format

created_by.description: Identifier of the user who created the application

default_branch.description: Git branch used for automatic and manual deployments when no branch is explicitly specified

display_name.description: Human-readable name shown in the dashboard and API responses

docker_context.description: Docker build context path relative to the repository root. Only applies when build type is `dockerfile`.

docker_image.description: Docker image reference including tag or digest. Only set for applications with `dockerImage` source.

docker_registry_credential_id.description: Identifier of the Docker registry credential used to pull the container image. Only applies to applications with `dockerImage` source.

dockerfile_path.description: Relative path to the Dockerfile within the repository. Only applies when build type is `dockerfile`.

git_lfs_enabled.description: When enabled, Git LFS objects are fetched during the source checkout step of a deployment. Enabled by default. Disable this to skip LFS downloads and speed up checkout when the repository contains LFS files that are not needed at build time.

git_type.description: Git hosting provider for the repository. `github` - GitHub. `bitbucket` - Bitbucket. `gitlab` - GitLab. Null for non-git sources.

hibernate_after_seconds.description: Number of seconds of inactivity before the application is hibernated. Only applies when hibernation is enabled.

hibernation_enabled.description: When enabled, the application automatically scales down to zero after a period of inactivity and wakes up on the next incoming request

ignore_deploy_paths.description: Glob patterns for file paths to exclude from deployment triggers. Commits that only touch ignored paths will not trigger auto deploy.

is_cdn_enabled.description: Whether the CDN is turned on for the application. Use the CDN toggle endpoint to change it. Null when the status is temporarily unavailable.

is_edge_cache_enabled.description: Whether edge caching is turned on for the application. Use the edge cache toggle endpoint to change it. Null when the status is temporarily unavailable.

is_suspended.description: Whether the application is currently suspended. Suspended applications have all processes stopped but retain their configuration.

name.description: Unique system name used in URLs and internal references. Auto-generated from the display name and cannot be changed after creation.

namespace.description: Kubernetes namespace where the application workloads run. Assigned automatically during creation.

nixpacks_version.description: Pinned Nixpacks version. When null, the platform default version is used. Only applies when build type is `nixpacks`.

pack_builder.description: Cloud Native Buildpacks builder image. Only applies when build type is `pack`.

project_id.description: Identifier of the project this application is grouped under

repo_url.description: Full URL of the Git repository. Null for Docker image source applications.

source.description: Where the application source code comes from. `privateGit` - private Git repository connected via OAuth. `publicGit` - public Git repository URL. `dockerImage` - Docker container image from a registry. `app` - pipeline promotion target with no Git repository or Docker image connected; deployments arrive by promoting from another pipeline stage.

status.description: Current status of the application reflecting the most recent deployment or lifecycle operation

type.description: Application type. `app` - standard application. `previewApp` - ephemeral preview environment created from a pull request.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the application was last modified, in ISO 8601 format

get.description: Retrieve HTTP access logs for an application. These are logs of incoming requests handled by the application. Returns the most recent `limit` entries in the time range, oldest first by default (set `order=desc` for newest first). Use `search` for a case-insensitive text match on the message, and `filters` for filtering by severity, message, tags, or attributes.

parameters.description: Start of the time range in ISO 8601 format. Defaults to 1 hour before `to` if not provided.
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: End of the time range in ISO 8601 format. Defaults to now if not provided.
parameters.name: to

parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the log message. Only entries whose message contains this text are returned. Can be combined with `filters`.
parameters.name: search

parameters.description:
JSON-encoded array of filter objects. All filters must match (they are combined with AND). Each filter has a `key`, an `operator`, and a `value` (or `values` for `IS_IN` and `IS_NOT_IN`).

Supported keys: `severity`, `message`, `id`, `tags.<name>` for a tag value, and `attributes.<name>` for an attribute value (use dots for nested attribute fields, e.g. `attributes.request.path`).

Supported operators: `EQUALS`, `DOES_NOT_EQUAL`, `CONTAINS`, `DOES_NOT_CONTAIN`, `STARTS_WITH`, `DOES_NOT_START_WITH`, `ENDS_WITH`, `DOES_NOT_END_WITH`, `GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUALS` and `LESS_THAN_OR_EQUALS` (numeric comparison), `IS_IN` and `IS_NOT_IN` (match against a list in `values`). Text operators are case-sensitive - use `search` for a case-insensitive message match. An unknown key or operator returns a 400.

Example: [{"key":"severity","operator":"IS_IN","values":["ERROR","WARN"]},{"key":"message","operator":"CONTAINS","value":"timeout"}]
parameters.name: filters

parameters.description: Sort order of the returned entries. `asc` - oldest first (default), `desc` - newest first. The order does not change which entries are returned: when more entries match than `limit`, the most recent ones are always returned.
parameters.name: order

parameters.description: Maximum number of log entries to return (1-5000). When more entries match, the most recent ones in the time range are returned.
parameters.name: limit

attributes.description: Additional structured attributes attached to the log entry

id.description: Unique identifier for the log entry

message.example: Server started on port 3000

service.description: Service that produced the log entry, such as APP_RUNTIME, APP_ACCESS, APP_DEPLOYMENT, SS_DEPLOYMENT, or SS_ACCESS

severity.description: Log severity level such as INFO, WARN, ERROR, or DEBUG

tags.description: Key-value pairs of tags associated with the log entry, such as container name or resource ID

timestamp.description: Formatted timestamp of the log entry

unix_timestamp.description: Unix timestamp of the log entry in microseconds

get.description: Retrieve a paginated list of all deployments for an application, ordered by most recent first. Each deployment includes its status, source details, and timestamps.

parameters.description: Maximum number of items per page
parameters.name: limit

app_id.description: Identifier of the application this deployment belongs to

author_img.description: Avatar URL of the Git commit author on the hosting provider

author_login.description: Username of the Git commit author on the hosting provider

branch.description: Git branch that was deployed. Null for Docker image deployments.

commit_message.description: Commit message of the deployed Git commit, truncated to 1000 characters

commit_sha.description: Full SHA hash of the Git commit that was deployed

created_at.description: Timestamp when the deployment was created, in ISO 8601 format

docker_image_url.description: Full URL of the Docker image built or used for this deployment, including the registry path and tag

finished_at.description: Timestamp when the deployment finished (succeeded, failed, or was cancelled), in ISO 8601 format. Null if still in progress.

git_type.description: Git hosting provider for the source repository. `github` - GitHub. `bitbucket` - Bitbucket. `gitlab` - GitLab. Null for Docker image deployments.

initiator_type.description: Who started the deployment. `USER` - a member of your company, from the dashboard or the API. `STAFF` - the Sevalla team, for example to roll out a required security update. The reason is in `note`. `AUTO_DEPLOY` - started automatically by a Git push, a deploy hook, or a new preview app. `SYSTEM` - started by Sevalla itself.

note.description: Why the Sevalla team started this deployment, for example `Required security update`. Only set when `initiator_type` is `STAFF`, otherwise null.

repo_url.description: Full URL of the Git repository used for this deployment. Null for Docker image deployments.

started_at.description: Timestamp when the deployment started executing, in ISO 8601 format. Null if still waiting.

status.description: Current status of the deployment in its lifecycle

steps.description: Ordered list of pipeline steps this deployment will execute. `checkout` - clone the repository. `build` - build the application image. `rollout` - deploy the image to the cluster. `syncConnections` - synchronize database and service connections.

trigger.description: Specific action that initiated the deployment, such as MANUAL_DEPLOY, ROLLBACK_DEPLOYMENT, AUTO_DEPLOY_ON_PUSH, or RESTART

type.description: How the deployment was initiated. `manual` - triggered by a user or API call. `automatic` - triggered automatically by a git push or webhook.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the deployment was last modified, in ISO 8601 format

total.description: Total number of items matching the query

post.description: Trigger a new deployment for an application. By default, deploys the latest commit on the default branch. You can optionally specify a different branch, a specific commit, a Docker image, or restart from the last successful deployment. You can also rebuild without the build cache. The deployment runs asynchronously - use the get deployment endpoint to track its progress.

branch.description: Git branch to deploy. When omitted, the application default branch is used. Only applies to Git-based applications.

commit_sha.description: Full 40 character SHA of the commit to deploy. When omitted, the latest commit on the branch is deployed. The commit must be reachable from `branch` (or the default branch when `branch` is omitted), otherwise the build fails at checkout. Its message and author are read from the repository; when they cannot be, the deployment records the SHA alone. Only applies to Git-based applications and cannot be combined with `is_restart`.

docker_image.description: Docker image reference to deploy (e.g., `nginx:latest`). Only applies to applications with `dockerImage` source.

is_restart.description: When true, redeploys using the existing build artifact from the last successful deployment, skipping the build step. Useful when you have updated runtime-level configuration and do not need to rebuild the application.

skip_build_cache.description: When true, every layer is rebuilt from scratch instead of being reused from the build cache. Use it to pick up updated system packages or dependencies that a cached build would keep. If the application has build cache enabled, the cache is refreshed with the new layers, so later builds do not fall back to the old ones. Only applies to Git-based applications and cannot be combined with `is_restart`.

commit_message.description: Commit message of the deployed Git commit, truncated to 1000 characters

get.description: Retrieve build and deployment logs for a specific deployment. These include output from the build process and rollout steps. Returns the most recent `limit` entries in the time range, oldest first by default (set `order=desc` for newest first). Use `search` for a case-insensitive text match on the message, and `filters` for filtering by severity, message, tags, or attributes.

parameters.description: Start of the time range in ISO 8601 format. Defaults to 1 hour before `to` if not provided.
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: End of the time range in ISO 8601 format. Defaults to now if not provided.
parameters.name: to

parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the log message. Only entries whose message contains this text are returned. Can be combined with `filters`.
parameters.name: search

parameters.description:
JSON-encoded array of filter objects. All filters must match (they are combined with AND). Each filter has a `key`, an `operator`, and a `value` (or `values` for `IS_IN` and `IS_NOT_IN`).

Supported keys: `severity`, `message`, `id`, `tags.<name>` for a tag value, and `attributes.<name>` for an attribute value (use dots for nested attribute fields, e.g. `attributes.request.path`).

Supported operators: `EQUALS`, `DOES_NOT_EQUAL`, `CONTAINS`, `DOES_NOT_CONTAIN`, `STARTS_WITH`, `DOES_NOT_START_WITH`, `ENDS_WITH`, `DOES_NOT_END_WITH`, `GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUALS` and `LESS_THAN_OR_EQUALS` (numeric comparison), `IS_IN` and `IS_NOT_IN` (match against a list in `values`). Text operators are case-sensitive - use `search` for a case-insensitive message match. An unknown key or operator returns a 400.

Example: [{"key":"severity","operator":"IS_IN","values":["ERROR","WARN"]},{"key":"message","operator":"CONTAINS","value":"timeout"}]
parameters.name: filters

parameters.description: Sort order of the returned entries. `asc` - oldest first (default), `desc` - newest first. The order does not change which entries are returned: when more entries match than `limit`, the most recent ones are always returned.
parameters.name: order

parameters.description: Maximum number of log entries to return (1-5000). When more entries match, the most recent ones in the time range are returned.
parameters.name: limit

attributes.description: Additional structured attributes attached to the log entry

id.description: Unique identifier for the log entry

message.example: Server started on port 3000

service.description: Service that produced the log entry, such as APP_RUNTIME, APP_ACCESS, APP_DEPLOYMENT, SS_DEPLOYMENT, or SS_ACCESS

severity.description: Log severity level such as INFO, WARN, ERROR, or DEBUG

tags.description: Key-value pairs of tags associated with the log entry, such as container name or resource ID

timestamp.description: Formatted timestamp of the log entry

unix_timestamp.description: Unix timestamp of the log entry in microseconds

put.description: Turn maintenance mode on or off for an application and optionally set a custom maintenance page URL. While enabled, every request to every domain of the application gets the maintenance page with status 503 and a Retry-After header instead of reaching the application. There are no path, method or visitor exceptions, and IP restrictions still apply first. The application keeps running and deployments still work. The change is written to the edge synchronously but can take up to 5 minutes to reach every location. Returns the updated state.

is_enabled.description: Whether maintenance mode should be active. When true, every request to every domain of the application receives the maintenance page with status 503. The application keeps running and can still be deployed while in maintenance mode.

page_url.description: HTTPS URL of a page to serve as the maintenance page, for example a Sevalla static site. The edge fetches the page body and serves it on every domain of the application with status 503, so visitors never see this URL. When null the default Sevalla maintenance page is served. Content changes on the page take up to 60 seconds to show. Must start with https:// and be at most 2048 characters. This is a full replace: when omitted or null, any previously set page URL is cleared and the default page is served.

post.description:
Run a single command inside a running application process (container) and return its output. This is a non-interactive alternative to the WebSocket terminal: one command runs, and its stdout, stderr, and exit code are returned. The command runs directly without a shell, so pipes, redirects, and command chaining do not apply.

This endpoint requires at least read access to the application. A key with only read access can run read-only commands (such as `ls`, `cat`, `env`, `ps`, `grep`); a request to run any other command is rejected with a 403. A key with write access to the application can run any command. Note that the read-only restriction is a convenience to prevent accidental changes, not a security sandbox: read-only commands can still read environment variables and files inside the container.

command.description: Command to run, given as an argument vector where the first element is the binary and the rest are its arguments (for example `["ls", "-la", "/app"]`). The command is run directly, not through a shell, so shell features like pipes, redirects, globbing, and chaining with `;` or `&&` are not available. Run those as separate calls instead. API keys with only read access to the application can run read-only commands (such as `ls`, `cat`, `env`, `ps`, `grep`); keys with write access can run any command.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the command to finish before it is aborted. Defaults to 15 seconds.

exit_code.description: Exit code returned by the command. `0` means success; any other value means the command failed.

stderr.description: Standard error produced by the command.

stdout.description: Standard output produced by the command.

get.description:
Open an interactive terminal (shell) session to a running application process.

**This is a WebSocket endpoint.** Connect using a WebSocket client with the `Upgrade: websocket` header. Standard HTTP requests return a `426 Upgrade Required` response.

### Connection

```
wscat -c "wss://api.sevalla.com/v3/applications/{id}/processes/{process_id}/terminal?shell=bash&cols=120&rows=40" -H "Authorization: Bearer <api_key>"
```

Authentication runs before the WebSocket upgrade - invalid credentials are rejected with a standard HTTP 401/403 response.

### Communication

Once connected, the WebSocket streams stdin/stdout bidirectionally to a shell running inside the container. Send text messages as shell input and receive command output as text messages.

### Terminal size

The terminal starts at the size given by the `cols` and `rows` query parameters, or 80x24 without them. To resize it, send a **binary** message holding the UTF-8 encoded JSON `{"type":"resize","cols":120,"rows":40}`. Sizes are clamped to 2-500 columns and 2-200 rows, and a resize message without integer `cols` and `rows` is ignored. Resize messages never reach the shell. Text messages are always shell input, even when they look like a resize message, and any other binary message is passed to the shell as input as well.

### Environment

The shell starts with `TERM=xterm-256color` and `COLORTERM=truecolor`. It also gets `LANG=C.UTF-8`, unless the container already sets `LANG` or an `LC_*` variable.

### Output

Output arrives as UTF-8 text messages. A character that the container writes in two pieces is always sent whole, never as a replacement character.

### Keepalive

The server sends a WebSocket ping every 25 seconds, which standard WebSocket clients answer with a pong on their own. This keeps an idle session open through proxies and load balancers. A connection that leaves two pings in a row unanswered is closed, and so is a session that has had no input and no output for 8 hours.

### Disconnects

A closed connection is not resumed, and the next connection starts a new shell. Run long jobs under `nohup`, or in `tmux` or `screen` when the image has them, so you can find them again after a disconnect.

### Close codes

- `4000` - Application or process not found
- `4001` - No running pod available to connect to
- `4002` - Shell stream error
- `4003` - Shell stream closed normally
- `4004` - No input and no output for 8 hours
- `4005` - Failed to connect to the pod
- `4300` - Unexpected server error

parameters.description: Shell to use for the terminal session. `sh` - Bourne shell (default). `bash` - Bourne Again Shell. `dash` - Debian Almquist Shell. `ksh` - KornShell. `zsh` - Z Shell. `csh` - C Shell. `tcsh` - TENEX C Shell.
parameters.name: shell

parameters.description: Width of the terminal in columns when the session starts, as an integer from 2 to 500. Values outside that range are clamped to it, and a missing or invalid value means 80. Send a resize message to change it later.
parameters.name: cols

parameters.description: Height of the terminal in rows when the session starts, as an integer from 2 to 200. Values outside that range are clamped to it, and a missing or invalid value means 24. Send a resize message to change it later.
parameters.name: rows

get.description: Retrieve runtime logs for an application. These are logs produced by the running application processes (stdout/stderr). Returns the most recent `limit` entries in the time range, oldest first by default (set `order=desc` for newest first). Use `search` for a case-insensitive text match on the message, and `filters` for filtering by severity, message, tags, or attributes.

parameters.description: Start of the time range in ISO 8601 format. Defaults to 1 hour before `to` if not provided.
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: End of the time range in ISO 8601 format. Defaults to now if not provided.
parameters.name: to

parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the log message. Only entries whose message contains this text are returned. Can be combined with `filters`.
parameters.name: search

parameters.description:
JSON-encoded array of filter objects. All filters must match (they are combined with AND). Each filter has a `key`, an `operator`, and a `value` (or `values` for `IS_IN` and `IS_NOT_IN`).

Supported keys: `severity`, `message`, `id`, `tags.<name>` for a tag value, and `attributes.<name>` for an attribute value (use dots for nested attribute fields, e.g. `attributes.request.path`).

Supported operators: `EQUALS`, `DOES_NOT_EQUAL`, `CONTAINS`, `DOES_NOT_CONTAIN`, `STARTS_WITH`, `DOES_NOT_START_WITH`, `ENDS_WITH`, `DOES_NOT_END_WITH`, `GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUALS` and `LESS_THAN_OR_EQUALS` (numeric comparison), `IS_IN` and `IS_NOT_IN` (match against a list in `values`). Text operators are case-sensitive - use `search` for a case-insensitive message match. An unknown key or operator returns a 400.

Example: [{"key":"severity","operator":"IS_IN","values":["ERROR","WARN"]},{"key":"message","operator":"CONTAINS","value":"timeout"}]
parameters.name: filters

parameters.description: Sort order of the returned entries. `asc` - oldest first (default), `desc` - newest first. The order does not change which entries are returned: when more entries match than `limit`, the most recent ones are always returned.
parameters.name: order

parameters.description: Maximum number of log entries to return (1-5000). When more entries match, the most recent ones in the time range are returned.
parameters.name: limit

attributes.description: Additional structured attributes attached to the log entry

id.description: Unique identifier for the log entry

message.example: Server started on port 3000

service.description: Service that produced the log entry, such as APP_RUNTIME, APP_ACCESS, APP_DEPLOYMENT, SS_DEPLOYMENT, or SS_ACCESS

severity.description: Log severity level such as INFO, WARN, ERROR, or DEBUG

tags.description: Key-value pairs of tags associated with the log entry, such as container name or resource ID

timestamp.description: Formatted timestamp of the log entry

unix_timestamp.description: Unix timestamp of the log entry in microseconds

put.description: Update the IP restriction configuration for a database. Sets the restriction type (allow or deny), enables or disables it, and updates the list of IP addresses or CIDR ranges. IP restrictions only apply to external connections. When type is `allow`, only the listed IPs can access the database. When type is `deny`, the listed IPs are blocked. For MySQL and MariaDB, a blocked client may still receive the initial server greeting because the server speaks first, but the connection is closed as soon as the client sends any data, so authentication can never complete. put.description: Update the preview stage configuration for a pipeline. You can set the preview app settings (cluster, build, processes, TCP proxies, disks, hibernation, environment variables), change the auto-create behavior and stale app cleanup, or switch the connected Git repository. Fields you leave out keep their current values, but preview_app replaces the whole preview app configuration. Turning on auto_create_app requires the preview app settings.

auto_create_app.description: Automatically create a preview app when a pull request is opened. Turning this on requires the preview app settings, either sent in preview_app or saved earlier. Returns 400 when they are missing.

delete_stale_apps.description: Automatically delete preview apps that have not been deployed for longer than the stale app threshold

preview_app.description: Configuration that every new preview app is created from. Sending it replaces the whole previous configuration, including anything set in the dashboard. Preview apps that already exist are not changed.

build_path.description: Relative path to the build directory within the repository. Defaults to the repository root.

build_type.description: Build strategy for preview apps. `nixpacks` - auto-detected build system. `railpack` - auto-detected build system, successor to Nixpacks. `dockerfile` - build using a Dockerfile. `pack` - build using Cloud Native Buildpacks. Defaults to `nixpacks`.

cluster_id.description: Identifier of the cluster (data center location) where preview apps are created.

docker_context.description: Docker build context path relative to the repository root. Only applies when build type is `dockerfile`.

dockerfile_path.description: Relative path to the Dockerfile within the repository. Only applies when build type is `dockerfile`.

environment_variables.description: Environment variables every preview app starts with. Each key can be used only once.

is_buildtime.description: Whether this variable is available during the build step. Defaults to true.

is_runtime.description: Whether this variable is available at runtime. Defaults to true.

key.description: Name of the environment variable. May contain only letters, digits, "-", "_", "." or ":".

value.description: Value of the environment variable. Stored encrypted at rest.

hibernate_after_seconds.description: Number of seconds of inactivity before a preview app is hibernated. Only applies when hibernation is enabled. Defaults to 300.

hibernation_enabled.description: Whether preview apps hibernate (scale down to zero) after a period of inactivity. Defaults to true. Must be false when any process uses horizontal scaling.

processes.description: Processes every preview app starts with. At most one can be a `web` process.

disk.description: Persistent disk the process gets on every preview app. Only web and worker processes can have a disk, and they must use manual scaling with at most one instance.

mount_path.description: Path inside the container where the disk is mounted. Only letters, numbers, `-`, `_`, `.` and `/` are allowed, and `/etc`, `/var`, `/lib`, `/usr/local`, `/mnt`, `/root`, `/app`, `/workspace` and `/layers` themselves cannot be used.

resource_type_id.description: Identifier of the disk resource type, which sets the disk size. Use the List Disk Resource Types endpoint to retrieve available options. A disk can grow but cannot shrink.

display_name.description: Human-readable name for the process shown in the dashboard. Cannot contain backticks, dollar signs, double quotes, backslashes or control characters.

entrypoint.description: Command used to start the process. If omitted, defaults to an empty string.

job_start_policy.description: When the job process should run relative to deployments. `beforeDeployment` - run after the build and before the new version of the other processes rolls out. If the job fails, the deployment fails and the running processes stay on the previous version. `afterSuccessDeployment` - run after a successful deployment. `afterFailedDeployment` - run after a failed deployment. Required for job processes.

post.description: Enable preview apps for a pipeline. When enabled, the pipeline can create ephemeral preview environments for pull requests. If the pipeline does not have a Git repository configured, you must provide a repo_url to connect one. Send preview_app to set the settings every preview app is created from (cluster, build, processes, TCP proxies, disks, hibernation, environment variables). If preview is already enabled, nothing changes - use the update preview settings endpoint instead.

auto_create_app.description: Automatically create a preview app when a pull request is opened. Requires preview_app. Returns 400 when true without it.

delete_stale_apps.description: Automatically delete preview apps that have not been deployed for longer than the stale app threshold

preview_app.description: Configuration that every new preview app is created from. Sending it replaces the whole previous configuration, including anything set in the dashboard. Preview apps that already exist are not changed.

build_path.description: Relative path to the build directory within the repository. Defaults to the repository root.

build_type.description: Build strategy for preview apps. `nixpacks` - auto-detected build system. `railpack` - auto-detected build system, successor to Nixpacks. `dockerfile` - build using a Dockerfile. `pack` - build using Cloud Native Buildpacks. Defaults to `nixpacks`.

cluster_id.description: Identifier of the cluster (data center location) where preview apps are created.

docker_context.description: Docker build context path relative to the repository root. Only applies when build type is `dockerfile`.

dockerfile_path.description: Relative path to the Dockerfile within the repository. Only applies when build type is `dockerfile`.

environment_variables.description: Environment variables every preview app starts with. Each key can be used only once.

is_buildtime.description: Whether this variable is available during the build step. Defaults to true.

is_runtime.description: Whether this variable is available at runtime. Defaults to true.

key.description: Name of the environment variable. May contain only letters, digits, "-", "_", "." or ":".

value.description: Value of the environment variable. Stored encrypted at rest.

hibernate_after_seconds.description: Number of seconds of inactivity before a preview app is hibernated. Only applies when hibernation is enabled. Defaults to 300.

hibernation_enabled.description: Whether preview apps hibernate (scale down to zero) after a period of inactivity. Defaults to true. Must be false when any process uses horizontal scaling.

processes.description: Processes every preview app starts with. At most one can be a `web` process.

disk.description: Persistent disk the process gets on every preview app. Only web and worker processes can have a disk, and they must use manual scaling with at most one instance.

mount_path.description: Path inside the container where the disk is mounted. Only letters, numbers, `-`, `_`, `.` and `/` are allowed, and `/etc`, `/var`, `/lib`, `/usr/local`, `/mnt`, `/root`, `/app`, `/workspace` and `/layers` themselves cannot be used.

resource_type_id.description: Identifier of the disk resource type, which sets the disk size. Use the List Disk Resource Types endpoint to retrieve available options. A disk can grow but cannot shrink.

display_name.description: Human-readable name for the process shown in the dashboard. Cannot contain backticks, dollar signs, double quotes, backslashes or control characters.

entrypoint.description: Command used to start the process. If omitted, defaults to an empty string.

job_start_policy.description: When the job process should run relative to deployments. `beforeDeployment` - run after the build and before the new version of the other processes rolls out. If the job fails, the deployment fails and the running processes stay on the previous version. `afterSuccessDeployment` - run after a successful deployment. `afterFailedDeployment` - run after a failed deployment. Required for job processes.

liveness_probe.description: Kubernetes liveness probe configuration. Only applicable to web processes.

command.description: Command to execute inside the container

exec.description: Exec-based probe - runs a command inside the container

failureThreshold.description: Minimum consecutive failures for the probe to be considered failed

name.description: Header name

httpHeaders.description: Custom headers to set in the request

path.description: Path to access on the HTTP server

port.description: Port number to access on the container

scheme.description: Scheme to use for connecting to the host. `HTTP` or `HTTPS`

httpGet.description: HTTP GET probe - performs an HTTP GET request

initialDelaySeconds.description: Seconds after the container starts before the probe is initiated

periodSeconds.description: How often in seconds to perform the probe

successThreshold.description: Minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful

port.description: Port number to connect to

tcpSocket.description: TCP socket probe - checks if a TCP port is open

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 120 when omitted.

port.description: Port number the process listens on for incoming connections

readiness_probe.description: Kubernetes readiness probe configuration. Only applicable to web processes.

exec.description: Exec-based probe - runs a command inside the container

resource_type_id.description: Identifier of the process resource type (machine size) to assign. Use the List Process Resource Types endpoint to retrieve available options.

type.description: Manual scaling type

scaleDownIncrement.description: Number of instances to remove per scale-down event

scaleDownIntervalSeconds.description: Cooldown period in seconds between scale-down events

scaleUpIncrement.description: Number of instances to add per scale-up event

scaleUpIntervalSeconds.description: Cooldown period in seconds between scale-up events

targetCpuPercent.description: Target CPU utilization percentage for autoscaling

targetMemoryPercent.description: Target memory utilization percentage for autoscaling

type.description: Horizontal auto-scaling type

schedule.description: Cron expression defining the execution schedule. Required for cron processes.

tcp_proxies.description: Ports of this process to expose on every preview app

is_public.description: Where the port is reachable. `true` - from the internet through a TCP proxy with its own public hostname and port. `false` - only from inside the cluster, as a private port. Defaults to false.

port.description: Container port of this process to expose

type.description: Process runtime type. `web` - HTTP server process that handles incoming web traffic. `worker` - background process that runs continuously. `cron` - scheduled process that runs at specified intervals. `job` - one-time process that runs to completion and then stops.

repo_url.description: Git repository URL to connect to the pipeline. Required if the pipeline does not already have a repository configured.

stale_app_days.description: Number of days after the last deployment before a preview app is considered stale

get.description: Retrieve HTTP access logs for a static site. These are logs of incoming requests served by the static site. Returns the most recent `limit` entries in the time range, oldest first by default (set `order=desc` for newest first). Use `search` for a case-insensitive text match on the message, and `filters` for filtering by severity, message, tags, or attributes.

parameters.description: Start of the time range in ISO 8601 format. Defaults to 1 hour before `to` if not provided.
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: End of the time range in ISO 8601 format. Defaults to now if not provided.
parameters.name: to

parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the log message. Only entries whose message contains this text are returned. Can be combined with `filters`.
parameters.name: search

parameters.description:
JSON-encoded array of filter objects. All filters must match (they are combined with AND). Each filter has a `key`, an `operator`, and a `value` (or `values` for `IS_IN` and `IS_NOT_IN`).

Supported keys: `severity`, `message`, `id`, `tags.<name>` for a tag value, and `attributes.<name>` for an attribute value (use dots for nested attribute fields, e.g. `attributes.request.path`).

Supported operators: `EQUALS`, `DOES_NOT_EQUAL`, `CONTAINS`, `DOES_NOT_CONTAIN`, `STARTS_WITH`, `DOES_NOT_START_WITH`, `ENDS_WITH`, `DOES_NOT_END_WITH`, `GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUALS` and `LESS_THAN_OR_EQUALS` (numeric comparison), `IS_IN` and `IS_NOT_IN` (match against a list in `values`). Text operators are case-sensitive - use `search` for a case-insensitive message match. An unknown key or operator returns a 400.

Example: [{"key":"severity","operator":"IS_IN","values":["ERROR","WARN"]},{"key":"message","operator":"CONTAINS","value":"timeout"}]
parameters.name: filters

parameters.description: Sort order of the returned entries. `asc` - oldest first (default), `desc` - newest first. The order does not change which entries are returned: when more entries match than `limit`, the most recent ones are always returned.
parameters.name: order

parameters.description: Maximum number of log entries to return (1-5000). When more entries match, the most recent ones in the time range are returned.
parameters.name: limit

attributes.description: Additional structured attributes attached to the log entry

id.description: Unique identifier for the log entry

message.example: Server started on port 3000

service.description: Service that produced the log entry, such as APP_RUNTIME, APP_ACCESS, APP_DEPLOYMENT, SS_DEPLOYMENT, or SS_ACCESS

severity.description: Log severity level such as INFO, WARN, ERROR, or DEBUG

tags.description: Key-value pairs of tags associated with the log entry, such as container name or resource ID

timestamp.description: Formatted timestamp of the log entry

unix_timestamp.description: Unix timestamp of the log entry in microseconds

get.description: Retrieve build and deployment logs for a specific static site deployment. These include output from the build process and publish steps. Returns the most recent `limit` entries in the time range, oldest first by default (set `order=desc` for newest first). Use `search` for a case-insensitive text match on the message, and `filters` for filtering by severity, message, tags, or attributes.

parameters.description: Start of the time range in ISO 8601 format. Defaults to 1 hour before `to` if not provided.
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: End of the time range in ISO 8601 format. Defaults to now if not provided.
parameters.name: to

parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the log message. Only entries whose message contains this text are returned. Can be combined with `filters`.
parameters.name: search

parameters.description:
JSON-encoded array of filter objects. All filters must match (they are combined with AND). Each filter has a `key`, an `operator`, and a `value` (or `values` for `IS_IN` and `IS_NOT_IN`).

Supported keys: `severity`, `message`, `id`, `tags.<name>` for a tag value, and `attributes.<name>` for an attribute value (use dots for nested attribute fields, e.g. `attributes.request.path`).

Supported operators: `EQUALS`, `DOES_NOT_EQUAL`, `CONTAINS`, `DOES_NOT_CONTAIN`, `STARTS_WITH`, `DOES_NOT_START_WITH`, `ENDS_WITH`, `DOES_NOT_END_WITH`, `GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUALS` and `LESS_THAN_OR_EQUALS` (numeric comparison), `IS_IN` and `IS_NOT_IN` (match against a list in `values`). Text operators are case-sensitive - use `search` for a case-insensitive message match. An unknown key or operator returns a 400.

Example: [{"key":"severity","operator":"IS_IN","values":["ERROR","WARN"]},{"key":"message","operator":"CONTAINS","value":"timeout"}]
parameters.name: filters

parameters.description: Sort order of the returned entries. `asc` - oldest first (default), `desc` - newest first. The order does not change which entries are returned: when more entries match than `limit`, the most recent ones are always returned.
parameters.name: order

parameters.description: Maximum number of log entries to return (1-5000). When more entries match, the most recent ones in the time range are returned.
parameters.name: limit

attributes.description: Additional structured attributes attached to the log entry

id.description: Unique identifier for the log entry

message.example: Server started on port 3000

service.description: Service that produced the log entry, such as APP_RUNTIME, APP_ACCESS, APP_DEPLOYMENT, SS_DEPLOYMENT, or SS_ACCESS

severity.description: Log severity level such as INFO, WARN, ERROR, or DEBUG

tags.description: Key-value pairs of tags associated with the log entry, such as container name or resource ID

timestamp.description: Formatted timestamp of the log entry

unix_timestamp.description: Unix timestamp of the log entry in microseconds
